# statcatlib

> statcatlib is a Python library for building, managing, and querying statistical metadata catalogs. It materializes remote catalog and structural metadata into a local catalog, a directory of products, each a chain of immutable editions held in DuckDB, and exposes a fluent Python API for discovery, filtering, full-text search, and provenance lineage. Designed to be embedded in ETL pipelines, data platforms, and analytical tooling.

Inspired by DCAT-AP, StatDCAT-AP, SDMX, DDI, and PROV-O. Pairs with [sdmxlib](https://github.com/StatCat-Suite/sdmxlib) for standards-aware workflows.

## Quick start

```python
import statcatlib as sc
import statcatlib.query as q
from sdmxlib import InternationalString as I18n
```

### Create a catalog, write a product, seal it

A catalog is a directory of products; each product is a chain of immutable editions. Writes go into a product's one unsealed edition, its `WorkingCopy`. Reads run on an `EditionView`.

```python
with sc.Catalog.create("my_catalog") as cat:           # exist_ok=True reopens an existing catalog for writing
    wc = cat.product("14100287").working_copy()         # start the product's one unsealed edition
    wc.put(dataset)                                     # write; sc.ingest_sdmx(wc, ...) and wc.registry too
    wc.view().get(sc.OpenDataset, "co2-2024")           # an EditionView that sees the working copy's writes
    edition = wc.seal()                                 # immutable edition, search index rebuilt, recorded live

with sc.Catalog.open("my_catalog") as cat:             # read-only
    view = cat.product("14100287").view()               # EditionView of the live edition
    view.get(sc.OpenDataset, "co2-2024")
```

- `wc.seal(checks=[sc.checks.conf_status()])` runs seal checks first; a finding raises `SealCheckError` and leaves the working copy open.
- `wc.discard()` throws the unsealed edition away. `wc.close()` (or leaving `with wc:`) keeps it unsealed; `product.working_copy(resume=True)` reopens it. A product has one working copy at a time.
- A view stays on its edition. `cat.refresh()`, then `cat.product(id).view()`, follows the live one. `cat.products()` lists products with a live edition; `product.editions()` lists the live edition.
- `Catalog.search` and `Catalog.facets` raise `NotImplementedError`; search and count one product's view.
- Throwaway catalog: `with statcatlib.testing.temporary_catalog() as cat: ...`
- In the examples below, `wc` is a `WorkingCopy` (writes) and `view` is an `EditionView` (reads). `wc.view()` has every read method too.

### Add datasets

```python
# Store a SKOS concept scheme before citing its concepts as themes
wc.put(sc.ConceptScheme(
    uri="urn:myorg:themes",
    label=I18n(en="My Themes"),
    concepts={"ENV": sc.Concept(notation="ENV", label=I18n(en="Environment"))},
))

wc.put(sc.OpenDataset(
    identifier="co2-2024",
    title=I18n(en="CO2 Emissions 2024"),
    description=I18n(en="Annual CO2 emissions by country"),
    publisher=sc.Agent(id="OECD", name=I18n(en="OECD")),
    themes=(sc.ConceptRef(uri="urn:myorg:themes/ENV"),),
    frequency=sc.Frequency(id="ANNUAL"),
    status="current",
))

wc.put([ds1, ds2, ds3])  # batch add — accepts list or tuple
```

### Direct lookup

```python
ds = view.get(sc.AggregateDataset, "ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(1.0)")
```

Returns `None` if not found or type doesn't match.

## Dataset kinds

Five concrete types, all inheriting from `BaseDataset`:

| Class | `kind` | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| `OpenDataset` | `"open"` | Generic datasets (CKAN, portals) |
| `AggregateDataset` | `"aggregate"` | Statistical tables with SDMX structure |
| `MicrodataDataset` | `"microdata"` | Survey/record-level data with variables |
| `GeospatialDataset` | `"geospatial"` | Spatial data with CRS and bounding box |
| `PublicationDataset` | `"publication"` | Articles, reports, analytical releases |

`sc.Dataset` is the union type alias. `sc.BaseDataset` is the generic bound.
`kind` is a `ClassVar` on each concrete class; `BaseDataset` has none.

### BaseDataset fields (shared by all kinds)

- `identifier: str` — unique key (required)
- `title: InternationalString` — bilingual title (required)
- `description: InternationalString` — bilingual description (required)
- `publisher: Agent | None`
- `contact_point: ContactPoint | None`
- `keywords: list[InternationalString]`
- `themes: tuple[ConceptRef, ...]`
- `dataset_type: ConceptRef | None`
- `subject: tuple[ConceptRef, ...]`
- `issued: datetime | None`
- `modified: datetime | None`
- `frequency: Frequency | None`
- `spatial_coverage: list[SpatialCoverage]`
- `temporal_coverage: TemporalCoverage | None`
- `distributions: list[Distribution]`
- `licence: LicenceDocument | None`
- `language: list[str]`
- `landing_page: str | None`
- `version: str | None`
- `status: str | None`
- `extras: dict[str, str]`

### AggregateDataset extra fields

- `dimension_names: list[InternationalString]` — human-readable dimension labels
- `num_series: int | None`
- `sdmx_dataflow_urn: str | None` — FK to sdmxlib's dataflows table
- `measure_dim: str | None` — default pivot axis for readers, recorded by `ingest_data()`

### MicrodataDataset extra fields

- `variables: list[Variable]` — variable-level metadata
- `sample_size: int | None`
- `universe: str | None`
- `collection_method: str | None`

### GeospatialDataset extra fields

- `crs: str | None` — e.g. `"EPSG:4326"`
- `spatial_resolution: str | None`
- `feature_types: list[str]`

### PublicationDataset extra fields

- `authors: list[str]`
- `doi: str | None`
- `isbn: str | None`
- `publication_type: str | None`
- `series_title: InternationalString | None`

## Supporting types

- `Agent(id, name, type, homepage)` — publisher or creator
- `ContactPoint(name, email, phone, url)`
- `Distribution(id, title, access_url, download_url, media_type, format, byte_size, ...)`
- `DataService(id, title, endpoint_url, serves_dataset, ...)`
- `Frequency(id, label)` — update frequency (e.g. `"ANNUAL"`, `"MONTHLY"`)
- `TemporalCoverage(start, end, label)`
- `SpatialCoverage(label, uri, bbox)`
- `LicenceDocument(id, label, uri)`
- `Variable(id, label, value_type, classification_id, ...)` — microdata variable
- `InternationalString(en="...", fr="...")` — bilingual string (from sdmxlib)

## SKOS types (themes and concept vocabularies)

statcatlib models themes as first-class SKOS artefacts. Two artefact types own data;
two ref types are lightweight pointers carried by datasets and catalogs.

- `ConceptScheme(uri, label, definition, concepts, top_concepts)` — a SKOS vocabulary.
  `concepts` maps `notation → Concept`. Store via `wc.put(scheme)`.
- `Concept(notation, label, alt_label, definition, broader, narrower, related)` — a SKOS
  concept within a scheme. `notation` is the local id; `broader`/`narrower`/`related`
  are notation strings within the same scheme.
- `ConceptRef(uri, scheme_uri, notation, label)` — typed pointer to a concept.
  Identity is the URI; `label`/`scheme_uri`/`notation` are denormalized hints.
  Carries on `Dataset.themes`, `.subject`, `.dataset_type`.
- `ConceptSchemeRef(uri, label)` — typed pointer to a concept scheme.
  Carries on `CatalogDescription.theme_taxonomy`.
- `is_concept_in_scheme(scheme, notation) -> bool` — pure-Python validation helper.

```python
# Store a concept scheme (cascades to concept rows)
wc.put(sc.ConceptScheme(
    uri="urn:sdmx:themes",
    label=I18n(en="Statistical Themes"),
    concepts={
        "ECONOMY": sc.Concept(notation="ECONOMY", label=I18n(en="Economy and finance")),
        "LABOUR":  sc.Concept(notation="LABOUR",  label=I18n(en="Labour market")),
    },
))

# Cite themes on a dataset (no automatic scheme creation)
ds = sc.OpenDataset(
    identifier="my-ds",
    title=I18n(en="My Dataset"),
    description=I18n(en="..."),
    themes=(sc.ConceptRef(uri="urn:sdmx:themes/ECONOMY"),),
)
```

`put(dataset)` writes only the `dataset_theme` bridge rows — it does not touch
the `concept` or `concept_scheme` tables. Store the `ConceptScheme` separately
before indexing so theme labels appear in BM25 search results.

## Query API

### QueryBuilder

`view.query(cls)` returns a `QueryBuilder[T]`. Builders are immutable: each method returns a new one, so calls chain.

```python
results = (
    view.query(sc.AggregateDataset)
    .filter(publisher="ESTAT", status="current")
    .search("unemployment quarterly")
    .include("publisher", "themes")   # load only these relationships
    .sort_by("modified", desc=True)
    .with_facets("themes", "frequency")
    .limit(10)
    .offset(0)
    .execute()
)

print(results.total)          # total matching count
print(results.items)          # list[AggregateDataset] for this page
print(results.facets)         # {"themes": {"Labour": 22, ...}, ...}
```

Terminal methods:

- `.execute() -> SearchResult[T]` — full result with items, total, facets
- `.collect() -> list[T]` — just the items (preferred, consistent with scopes)
- `.all() -> list[T]` — alias for `.collect()`
- `.first() -> T | None` — first match or None
- `.one() -> T` — exactly one match (raises otherwise)
- `.count() -> int` — total count
- `.exists() -> bool` — True if at least one match (no object reconstruction)

### Selective relationship loading

By default all relationships are loaded (~17 queries per list call). Use
`.include()` to declare exactly which ones to batch-load — the rest are set
to an `UNLOADED` sentinel. Use `.full()` to revert to loading everything.

```python
# 3 batch queries instead of ~17
view.query(sc.BaseDataset).include("publisher", "themes", "keywords").all()

# Explicit full hydration
view.query(sc.BaseDataset).full().all()

# get() is always fully loaded — no .include() needed
view.get(sc.AggregateDataset, "ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(1.0)")
```

Unloaded fields raise `sc.NotLoadedError` (subclass of `AttributeError`) on
access. Use `sc.is_unloaded(value)` to check before accessing:

```python
ds = view.query(sc.BaseDataset).include("publisher").first()
ds.publisher.name    # OK — was included
ds.themes[0]         # NotLoadedError: 'themes' was not loaded
                     #   Add 'themes' to .include() or call .full()

if not sc.is_unloaded(ds.themes):
    for t in ds.themes:
        print(t.label)
```

Valid names (match model field names): `publisher`, `contact_point`, `frequency`,
`licence`, `themes`, `subject`, `dataset_type`, `keywords`, `spatial_coverage`,
`distributions`, `conforms_to`, `quality_annotations`, `provenance`,
`dimension_names`, `variables`, `feature_types`, `authors`.

### Projection modifiers

When you only need a few columns, projection modifiers bypass full object
reconstruction (single SQL query):

```python
# Row projection — .select() returns Row objects (dict subclass with attribute access)
rows = (
    view.query(sc.BaseDataset)
    .filter(q.title_contains("GDP"))
    .sort_by("title", lang="en")
    .limit(3)
    .select("identifier", "title", lang="en")
    .rows()
)
# → [Row({"identifier": "GDP", "title": "GDP Growth"}), ...]
rows[0].identifier   # attribute-style access
rows[0]["title"]     # dict-style access — both work
isinstance(rows[0], dict)  # True

# Flat value projection — .scalars() returns bare values
ids = view.query(sc.BaseDataset).filter(status="current").scalars("identifier").values()
# → ["EXR", "M1", "UNEMP", ...]

# .row() is the single-row terminal; .first() and .one() raise ValueError under a projection
row = view.query(sc.BaseDataset).filter(identifier="EXR").select("identifier", "title", lang="en").row()
# → Row({"identifier": "EXR", "title": "Exchange Rate EUR/USD"})
```

Selectable columns: `identifier`, `kind`, `status`, `issued`, `modified`, `landing_page`, `version`, `title` (MAP, requires `lang`), `description` (MAP, requires `lang`).

`sc.Row` is a `dict` subclass — `isinstance(row, dict)` is `True`, JSON serialisation works normally.

### Seeding with IDs

```python
view.query(sc.BaseDataset).from_ids(["ID1", "ID2", "ID3"]).all()
```

### Field filters (keyword arguments)

```python
.filter(publisher="ESTAT")
.filter(status="current")
.filter(frequency="MONTHLY")
.filter(identifier="ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(1.0)")
```

### Composable filter objects (`statcatlib.query`)

```python
import statcatlib.query as q

# Code filter — datasets with GEO=DE in their codelist
q.has_code("geo", "DE")

# Hierarchy descent — any code *under* CA. Strict: CA itself does not match;
# pass include_self=True to widen. The applicable Hierarchy is resolved per
# dataflow (sdmx.hierarchy_applicability), falling back to the codelist's own
# parent chain. Equivalent spellings:
q.within("REF_AREA", "CA")
q.has_code("REF_AREA", q.descendants_of("CA"))
q.within("REF_AREA", "CA", hierarchy=h_admin)   # descend a named Hierarchy

# Dimension filter — datasets with both GEO and FREQ dimensions
q.has_dimensions(["geo", "freq"])

# Distribution filter — datasets with a CSV distribution
q.distribution(format="CSV")
q.distribution(media_type="application/zip")

# Service filter — datasets served by a specific endpoint
q.has_service(endpoint_url="https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest")

# MAP column filters — spatial, keyword, title, description
q.has_spatial("Canada")                    # spatial coverage label match
q.has_spatial("Ontario", lang="en")
q.has_keyword("employment")               # keyword match
q.title_contains("GDP")                   # case-insensitive ILIKE on title
q.description_contains("quarterly")       # case-insensitive ILIKE on description
```

All filters are ANDed:

```python
view.query(sc.AggregateDataset).filter(
    q.has_code("geo", "DE"),
    q.has_dimensions(["geo", "freq"]),
    q.distribution(format="CSV"),
    publisher="ECB",
    status="current",
).all()
```

### Sorting by MAP columns

```python
# Sort by multilingual title (requires lang parameter)
view.query(sc.BaseDataset).sort_by("title", lang="en").all()
view.query(sc.BaseDataset).sort_by("title", lang="en", desc=True).all()
```

### Cross-entity queries

```python
# Agents that publish aggregate datasets with GEO=CA
view.query(sc.Agent).filter(
    q.publishes(q.has_code("geo", "CA"), kind="aggregate")
).all()

# Data services serving aggregate datasets
view.query(sc.DataService).filter(
    q.serves(kind="aggregate")
).all()
```

## Full-text search

A dataset's search text holds its title, description and keywords, plus its theme labels and dimension names, so BM25 also finds datasets by classification metadata.

```python
# Standalone BM25 search over datasets, concepts and codes; each item is a Hit
results = view.search("gross domestic product", kinds=("dataset",), limit=10)
results.items[0].payload.identifier

# Combined with filters via QueryBuilder
results = (
    view.query(sc.AggregateDataset)
    .filter(publisher="ESTAT")
    .search("labour force")
    .execute()
)
```

## Semantic and hybrid search

Requires an embedding model on the view (install with `statcatlib[search]`):

```python
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

model = SentenceTransformer("intfloat/multilingual-e5-small")
view = cat.product("14100287").view(embedding_model=model)   # query_prefix= too; BM25 needs no model

# Pure vector search — returns Hit objects; hit.payload is the dataset
results = view.datasets.find("people moving between provinces", mode="vector")

# Hybrid BM25 + vector (RRF fusion) — recommended
results = view.datasets.find("labour market monthly data", mode="hybrid", limit=20)

# Hybrid via QueryBuilder with filters
results = (
    view.query(sc.AggregateDataset)
    .filter(status="current")
    .hybrid_search("unemployment trends")
    .limit(20)
    .execute()
)
```

Build the index of a working copy, so `wc.view()` can search before the seal:

```python
n = wc.build_index()  # returns count of datasets indexed
# Uses batch encoding (256 texts per encode() call) and bulk LanceDB writes
n = wc.build_index(embedding_model=model)  # with vector embeddings
```

`wc.seal()` rebuilds the index from the edition's rows with the arguments of the last `wc.build_index()` call, or the defaults when there was none. CLI: `statcat build-index CATALOG PRODUCT [options]` resumes the product's working copy, builds its index, and leaves it unsealed.

## Facets

```python
# Global facet counts
counts = view.facets("publisher", "themes", "frequency", "status", "type", "spatial")
# {"publisher": {"ESTAT": 42, ...}, "themes": {"Labour": 22, ...}, ...}

# In-context facets (filtered)
results = (
    view.query(sc.AggregateDataset)
    .filter(publisher="ESTAT")
    .with_facets("themes", "frequency")
    .execute()
)
print(results.facets["themes"])
```

### Facet label resolution

Publisher and theme facets return IDs. Use label methods for display names:

```python
view.agent_labels(lang="en")    # {"ESTAT": "Eurostat", "ECB": "European Central Bank", ...}
view.concept_labels(lang="en")  # {"<concept uri>": "Economy and finance", ...}
view.spatial_labels(lang="en")  # {"Canada": "Canada", ...}
```

## Source connectors

### SDMX (Eurostat, OECD, BIS, ABS, ECB, ...)

```python
import sdmxlib as sl

with sc.Catalog.create("my_catalog", exist_ok=True) as cat:
    with cat.product("estat").working_copy() as wc:
        with sl.RestRegistry(sl.Provider.ESTAT) as reg:
            reg.get(sl.Dataflow.urn_for(agency="ESTAT", id="NAMA_10_GDP"), resolve=True)
            sc.ingest_sdmx(wc, reg.registry)

            # With publisher/theme overrides
            publisher = sc.Agent(id="ESTAT", name=I18n(en="Eurostat"))
            sc.ingest_sdmx_registry(wc, reg.registry, publisher=publisher)

            # Write observations to the edition's DuckLake (long layout) and bind them to the dataflow
            sc.ingest_data(wc, reg, "ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(latest)", measure_dim="na_item")
        wc.seal()
```

Every ingest function takes a `WorkingCopy` and raises `TypeError` for an `EditionView`. SDMX structures and observations go through `wc.registry` (`wc.registry.ingest(...)`, `wc.registry.write_observations(...)`).

### CKAN (open.canada.ca, data.gov, ...)

```python
with sc.Catalog.create("my_catalog", exist_ok=True) as cat:
    with cat.product("open-canada").working_copy() as wc:
        sc.ingest_ckan(wc, "https://open.canada.ca/data", organization="statcan-statcan", limit=500)
        wc.seal()
```

## Lineage and provenance (PROV-O)

```python
# Record a derivation relationship, in a working copy
wc.add_lineage(
    source_id="lfs-microdata",
    target_id="14100287",
    relationship="aggregated_from",
    activity_type="aggregation",
    activity_label="LFS monthly tabulation",
    confidence="asserted",  # or "extracted", "inferred"
)

# Transitive traversal on a view — returns QueryBuilder, chain before materialising
ancestors = view.dataset("14100287").upstream(depth=5).collect()
dependents = view.dataset("CL_GEO").downstream(relationship="uses_classification").collect()

# Chain filters after traversal
current = view.dataset("14100287").upstream().filter(status="current").collect()

# Inspect records
rows = view.dataset("14100287").lineage_records(role="target", relationship="aggregated_from")
```

Relationship vocabulary: `derived_from`, `aggregated_from`, `adjusted_from`, `revision_of`, `supplement_to`, `feeds_into`, `uses_classification`, `replaces`.

## Scope-based graph traversal

Scopes are lazy handles representing positions in the catalog graph. Navigation builds scope objects without executing SQL; only terminal methods (`.collect()`, `.count()`) hit the database.

```python
import statcatlib as sc

# Navigate theme schemes
view.themes.collect()                              # list[SchemeScope]
view.themes["subjects"].collect()                   # ItemList[Concept]
view.themes["subjects"]["13"].collect()             # Concept

# Cross-entity navigation — .datasets returns a lazy QueryBuilder
view.themes["subjects"]["13"].datasets.collect()    # list[BaseDataset]
view.themes["subjects"].datasets.limit(10).collect()

# Codelist navigation — use sc.urn helpers to build URN strings
view.codelist(sc.urn.codelist("SDMX", "CL_GEO")).collect()          # ItemList[Code]
view.codelist(sc.urn.codelist("SDMX", "CL_GEO"))["ON"].collect()    # Code
view.codelist(sc.urn.codelist("SDMX", "CL_GEO")).datasets.collect() # datasets using this codelist

# CodelistsScope — supports enrich with labels, lang, and text filtering
view.codelists.lang("en").enrich(n=sc.each("datasets").count()).collect()
# → [{"urn": "...", "label": "Geography", "n": 5}, ...]

# Filter codelists by label text (SQL-level, case-insensitive)
view.codelists.filter(text_contains="geo").enrich(n=sc.each("datasets").count()).collect()

view.codelist(urn).label("en")   # quick name lookup

# Enriched per-code output includes code name labels
view.codelist(urn).lang("en").enrich(n=sc.each("datasets").count()).collect()
# → [{"code_id": "ON", "label": "Ontario", "n": 5}, ...]

# Batch label resolution — single SQL query for many codes
view.codelist(geo_urn).batch_labels(["CA", "US", "DE"])
# → {"CA": "Canada", "US": "United States", "DE": "Germany"}

# Across multiple codelists in one query
view.codelists.batch_labels([(geo_urn, "CA"), (freq_urn, "A")], lang="en")
# → {(geo_urn, "CA"): "Canada", (freq_urn, "A"): "Annual"}

# Dimension traversal
dims = view.dimensions(ds).collect()              # ItemList[DimensionInfo]
codelist = view.dimensions(ds)["GEO"].codelist    # CodelistScope | None
```

### Sub-traversal expressions (`sc.each`)

`sc.each("edge")` creates a context-free sub-traversal expression (like `pl.col()` in Polars). Reusable across `.enrich()`, `.filter()`, and `.sort_by()`.

```python
n_datasets = sc.each("datasets").count()
has_data = sc.each("datasets").exists()

# Enrich each concept with dataset counts
view.themes["subjects"].enrich(n=n_datasets).collect()

# Multiple enrichments
view.themes["subjects"].enrich(
    sc.each("datasets").count().alias("total"),
    sc.each("datasets").filter(status="current").count().alias("current"),
).collect()

# Filter, enrich, and sort — all lazy until .collect()
view.themes["subjects"] \
    .filter(has_data) \
    .enrich(n=n_datasets) \
    .sort_by(n_datasets, desc=True) \
    .collect()
```

### Scope classes

| Scope | Entry point | `.collect()` returns |
|---|---|---|
| `ThemesScope` | `view.themes` | `list[SchemeScope]` |
| `SchemeScope` | `view.themes["id"]` | `ItemList[Concept]` |
| `ConceptScope` | `view.themes["id"]["cid"]` | `Concept` |
| `CodelistsScope` | `view.codelists` | `list[CodelistScope]` |
| `CodelistScope` | `view.codelist("urn")` | `ItemList[Code]` |
| `CodeScope` | `view.codelist("urn")["id"]` | `Code` |
| `DimensionsScope` | `view.dimensions(ds)` | `ItemList[DimensionInfo]` |
| `DimensionScope` | `view.dimensions(ds)["GEO"]` | `DimensionInfo` |

All collection scopes (ThemesScope, SchemeScope, CodelistsScope, CodelistScope, DimensionsScope) support `.enrich()`, `.filter()`, `.sort_by()`. Single-item scopes (ConceptScope, CodeScope, DimensionScope) have `.collect()` and navigation only. `CodelistScope` also has `.label(lang)` for quick name lookup.

`CodelistsScope` supports `.lang(lang)` and `.filter(text_contains=)` for SQL-level label resolution and text filtering. Enriched `.collect()` includes a `label` field (via `sdmx.localized_text`).

`CodelistScope` supports `.lang(lang)`. Enriched `.collect()` includes a `label` field from the code's `name` MAP column (falls back to `code_id`).

### Expression terminals

| Method | Returns | SQL |
|---|---|---|
| `.count()` | int per item | `COUNT(*)` |
| `.exists()` | bool per item | `EXISTS(...)` |
| `.sum("field")` | numeric per item | `SUM(field)` |
| `.ids()` | list[str] per item | `LIST(id)` |
| `.count_distinct()` | int per item | `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)` |

## Structural traversal (convenience methods)

For `AggregateDataset` records linked to SDMX structural metadata:

```python
# Dimension → code → label mapping
codes = view.code_map("ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(1.0)", lang="en")
# {"na_item": {"B1GQ": "Gross domestic product at market prices", ...}, "geo": {"AT": "Austria", ...}}

# Full sdmxlib Codelist object
cl = view.codelist_for("ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(1.0)", "geo")

# DSD (Data Structure Definition)
dsd = view.get_structure(view.get(sc.AggregateDataset, "ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(1.0)"))

# Impact analysis — datasets sharing a codelist
affected = view.codelists["urn:sdmx:...Codelist=ESTAT:CL_GEO(1.0)"].datasets.execute().items
related = view.dataset("ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(1.0)").related("codelist")

# Direct sdmxlib access to the read surface (get, query, obs) over the same edition
reg = view.registry
```

## Reading observations

`ingest_data()` registers an sdmxlib `DataflowBinding` for the table it writes,
so the edition's registry reads it back. The query is lazy until a terminal;
`.frame()` and `.pivot()` return a `polars.DataFrame` typed from the DSD.

```python
import sdmxlib as sl

ds = view.get(sc.AggregateDataset, "ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(1.0)")
obs = view.registry.obs(sl.Dataflow.parse_urn(ds.sdmx_dataflow_urn))

annual_de = obs.filter(obs.col("freq") == "A", obs.col("geo") == "DE").frame()  # long
wide = obs.pivot(on=ds.measure_dim)  # one column per code of the pivot axis
```

## URN helpers (`statcatlib.urn`)

SDMX URNs are long strings like `urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.codelist.Codelist=SDMX:CL_GEO(1.0)`. The `sc.urn` module provides shorthand builders:

```python
import statcatlib as sc

sc.urn.codelist("SDMX", "CL_GEO", "1.0")
# → "urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.codelist.Codelist=SDMX:CL_GEO(1.0)"

sc.urn.dataflow("ESTAT", "NAMA_10_GDP", "1.0")
# → "urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.datastructure.Dataflow=ESTAT:NAMA_10_GDP(1.0)"

sc.urn.data_structure("ESTAT", "DSD_NAMA", "1.0")
sc.urn.concept_scheme("SDMX", "CS_FREQ", "1.0")

# Version defaults to "1.0"
sc.urn.codelist("SDMX", "CL_GEO")

# Parse a URN back into components
parsed = sc.urn.parse("urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.codelist.Codelist=SDMX:CL_GEO(1.0)")
parsed.agency       # "SDMX"
parsed.id           # "CL_GEO"
parsed.version      # "1.0"
```

Use with view APIs:

```python
view.codelist(sc.urn.codelist("SDMX", "CL_GEO")).collect()
view.codelists[sc.urn.codelist("ESTAT", "CL_GEO")].datasets.execute().items
```

## Architecture

Each edition holds three layers in one DuckDB database and its DuckLake:

- **Discovery layer** (statcatlib, `statcat` schema) — dataset, agent, concept_scheme, concept, distribution, lineage
- **Structural layer** (sdmxlib, `sdmx` schema) — dataflow, data_structure, codelist, code
- **Observation layer** (DuckLake tables, bound to dataflows) — actual time-series data, read with `view.registry.obs(flow)`

The catalog's files (`catalog.json`, the Inventory, one directory per edition) are specified in the Catalog Format page of the docs; callers reach them only through the API.

statcatlib queries JOIN freely across both its own tables and sdmxlib's tables. The `sdmx_dataflow_urn` field on `AggregateDataset` is the foreign key that links the two. `has_code()` and `has_dimensions()` JOIN through sdmxlib's structural tables (only work for datasets that have `sdmx_dataflow_urn` set via SDMX ingest).

## Public API (`statcatlib.__all__`)

### Model types
`Agent`, `AggregateDataset`, `BaseDataset`, `CatalogDescription`, `CatalogRecord`, `Concept`, `ConceptRef`, `ConceptScheme`, `ConceptSchemeRef`, `ContactPoint`, `DataService`, `Dataset`, `DatasetT`, `Distribution`, `Frequency`, `GeospatialDataset`, `InternationalString`, `LicenceDocument`, `MicrodataDataset`, `OpenDataset`, `ProvenanceStatement`, `PublicationDataset`, `QualityAnnotation`, `SpatialCoverage`, `Standard`, `StatisticalDataset`, `TemporalCoverage`, `Variable`, `is_concept_in_scheme`

### Catalog, views and scopes
`Catalog`, `Product`, `Edition`, `WorkingCopy`, `EditionView`, `QueryBuilder`, `Row`, `SearchResult`, `ConceptSchemesScope`, `ConceptSchemeScope`, `ThemesScope`, `SchemeScope`, `ConceptScope`, `CodelistsScope`, `CodelistScope`, `CodeScope`, `DimensionsScope`, `DimensionScope`, `DimensionInfo`

### Sentinels and error types
`NotLoadedError`, `is_unloaded`, `IncompatibleCatalogError`, `IncompatibleIndexError`, `NoLiveEditionError`, `WorkingCopyExistsError`, `WorkingCopyClosedError`, `SealCheckError`, `JournalError`, `InventoryConflictError`, `InventoryContentionError`, `InventoryRuleError`, `NonFastForwardError`

### Seal checks (`statcatlib.checks`)
`conf_status`, `SealCheck`

### Expression language (`statcatlib.expr`)
`each`, `Expr`, `TraversalExpr`, `CountExpr`, `ExistsExpr`, `AliasedExpr`

### URN helpers (`statcatlib.urn`)
`codelist`, `dataflow`, `data_structure`, `concept_scheme`, `parse`

### Source functions
`dataset_from_dataflow`, `ingest_ckan`, `ingest_data`, `ingest_sdmx`, `ingest_sdmx_registry`, `prepare_sdmx`

### Query filters (`statcatlib.query`)
`has_code`, `has_dimensions`, `distribution`, `has_service`, `publishes`, `serves`, `has_spatial`, `has_keyword`, `title_contains`, `description_contains`, `ExistsFilter`, `MapCondition`, `MapFilter`, `PositionalFilter`
